steps.title: Look at the four sentences again.
steps.sub: He has found his mother. · He found her in 2011.
steps.prompt: When do we use the Past Simple instead of the Present Perfect?
options: When we say the finished time: in 2011, yesterday, when he was five.
When the story is sad, or when it ended badly for somebody.
When we are speaking to somebody rather than writing to them.
steps.answer: When we say the finished time: in 2011, yesterday, when he was five.
steps.why: A finished time expression forces the Past Simple. Without one, an experience or a result takes the Present Perfect.

steps.title: Present Perfect or Past Simple?
steps.html:
Present Perfect — no finished timePast Simple — finished time
He has found his mother again.He found her in 2011.
He has been to university.He studied there from 2005 to 2008.
Have you ever lived abroad?Did you live in Almaty last year?
She has never spoken about it.She didn’t speak for some time.
I’ve read his book.I read it in the summer.

Present Perfect = have / has + past participle: found, been, done, written. Irregular participles must be learned: go – went – gone.

Use the Present Perfect for an experience at some time in your life (ever, never) or for a past action with a result now.

Use the Past Simple as soon as you say when: yesterday, in 2011, last year, when he was five, two hours ago.

Very common mistake: I have seen him yesterday. With yesterday it must be I saw him yesterday.

just, already and yet come in the next lesson; for and since come back in Unit 12.

steps.prompt: Why does the speaker use “he’s written a book” and not “he wrote a book”?
options: There is no finished time — the book exists now.
Because the book is short and easy to read.
Because it all happened a very long time ago.
steps.answer: There is no finished time — the book exists now.

steps.title: Write about three experiences in your life.

steps.html:
1. Plan: the experience (Present Perfect) → when and where it happened (Past Simple) → how it was.

  • It happened in …
  • I’ve never …
  • I’ve been to …
  • I went there in …
  • The best one was …
